correctness.rationale: Finite-cell log form: diagonal 2 gamma-2-2logN, off-diagonal c_k; d_k=c_k-1/k strictly positive with total 1-gamma. Polarization yields exact identity with nonnegative summable shift error. Uniform-vector lower bound and uniform shift remainder bound give bounded-below continuum logarithmic form of Perron histograms, whence Fourier tightness and strong L2 compactness. Shift continuity removes remainder. Upper semicontinuity plus dense smooth step tests proves the exact additive limit. The previously established Chen–Weth theorem gives uniqueness/positivity of the continuum maximizer and thus full-sequence convergence. Normalization and finite identity are rechecked by an embedded standalone stdlib script; no finite check is substituted for an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Lee–Dai–Bettelheim treats eigenvalue distribution and one jump, whereas the target has an unbounded logarithmic singularity at one point and concerns its isolated top edge. Zhu–Wakin explicitly assumes uniformly bounded Toeplitz matrices in its general asymptotic-equivalence statement, not satisfied by ||A_N||~2log N. Chen–Weth studies fractional Laplacian limits, not this discrete path discretization.

originality.rationale: The 2011 initiating source (Li–Villavert) gives explicit upper and lower bounds of form \(2\log N+O(1)\) for the identical matrix; Cheng–Li (2013) adds finite Perron uniqueness and qualitative symmetry/monotonicity. This result identifies the additive limit with an already-known continuum logarithmic-Laplacian first eigenvalue, proves strong convergence of rescaled Perron vectors to the known ground state, and supplies a new finite positive cell remainder. The continuum eigenvalue simplicity of Chen–Weth is prior input, not newly claimed; no inspected source covers the discrete-to-continuum theorem. An inaccessible plausible Wiley Harary paper and a possible general unlocated Toeplitz-edge theorem are material residual risks.
residual_risks: The full Wiley article DOI 10.1002/qua.21558 was not materially accessible; its abstract alone cannot establish noncoverage.
A broader theorem for unbounded logarithmic Toeplitz symbols or path Harary matrices may imply the same limit without matching terminology.
The continuum ground-state theory itself is known; novelty attaches only to its identification as the discrete additive spectral limit and corresponding Perron profile.

value.rationale: Li–Villavert (2011) and Cheng–Li (2013) specifically studied the critical reciprocal-distance path operator, proving only leading \(2\log N\) growth with bounded unknown correction. The exact additive spectral constant and strong limiting optimizer identify a complete natural infinite-size invariant and its continuum spectral geometry. The all-N positive remainder makes the mechanism structurally meaningful and reusable for discretization questions. This is neither a routine numerical estimate nor a repackaged claim that the continuum first eigenfunction exists.
